note.fact: For natural a,r, the product (a+1)⋯(a+r), with empty product 1, equals r! * Nat.choose (a+r) r. Consequently its complex value divided by r! is the natural integer binom(a+r,r). Apply this with a=λ-i for the X formula (r≤i), and a=i for the Y formula (i+r≤λ).
note.justification: The probed theorem gives exactly (a+1).ascFactorial r = r!*(a+r).choose r; the read definition of ascFactorial is the displayed rising product. Since i∈I implies 0≤i≤λ, both substitutions have nonnegative integer a, and r is nonnegative by the X/Y domains. Factorial r is a product of positive integers, so its complex cast is nonzero and can be cancelled. Nat.choose is natural-valued, hence an integer after casting. This checks the routine product-to-binomial identification and integrality asserted in S004, without replacing the locally proved action recurrences or basis argument.

have e0 : LR.e y v 0 = v := by simp [LR.e, LR.DP]
have ya (i : ℕ) : y (LR.e y v i) = ((i+1 : ℕ) : ℂ) • LR.e y v (i+1) := by
  simp only [LR.e, LR.DP, LinearMap.smul_apply, map_smul]

  rw [Nat.factorial_succ, Nat.cast_mul, smul_smul]

  have hsub : ((lam.toNat-(j+1)+1 : ℕ):ℂ) = (lam.toNat : ℂ) - j := by
    push_cast [Nat.cast_sub (show j+1 ≤ lam.toNat from hil)]
    ring
  simp only [Int.cast_mul, Int.cast_natCast, Int.cast_sub, Nat.factorial_succ, Nat.cast_mul, smul_smul]

  field_simp
